In general, patients should be assessed for nutrient deficien-
cies before supplementation is initiated. In all newly diagnosed 
patients, the clinician should consider checking levels of ferri-
tin, red blood cell folate, and 25-OH vitamin D. If patients pres-
ent with more severe symptoms, such as diarrhea, weight loss, 
malabsorption, or signs of nutrient deficiencies (e.g., night-
blindness, neuropathy, prolonged prothrombin time), other 
vitamins such as fat-soluble vitamins (A, E, K) and minerals 
(zinc) should be checked.
